mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during confirmed rising rate periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 2% relative to the prior month predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market expansion supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS growth (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1400 units in two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is positive, reflecting stronger consumer demand anticipation.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the trigger being met (out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals contraction risks.
failure_condition: No significant negative returns when INDPRO declines >5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining CPIAUCSL (CPI) below 253.0 are associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as deflation expectations reduce real discount rates.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive during confirmed deflationary episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE (unemployment rate) and a decline in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 1% suggests labor market stress and predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return via risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >= 1% while PAYEMS decreases by >= 1% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in such interaction events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows by at least 4% over the prior quarter, the S&P 60-day forward return is positive, reflecting strong aggregate demand.
failure_condition: No positive 60-day forward returns when GDPC1 grows >=4% (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (commercial loan growth) for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as credit availability contraction signals economic weakness.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative during confirmed credit contraction (p > 0.05).
